note: KDWP state fishing lake: a 300-acre lake in the canyon country of Clark County, south of Kingsdown on K-94. Camping is allowed throughout the area, with four named primitive camping/day-use areas: South End (at the dam), East Shore (a gravel loop on a point and a gravel lane along the shore, off K-94), Bloom Cove (west shore, by county gravel road) and North End (upper end). No marked sites. Boats for fishing only. --Claude
summary: KDWP Clark page (Wayback 2026-07-11): 300-acre lake, camping allowed throughout, four primitive camping/day-use areas, four ramps with restrooms; free and FCFS (KDWP camping page); max stay 7 nights per K.A.R. 115-8-9(c) (newly written). Phone missing -> 620-227-8609. Waterfront lead not waterfront -> lakeview+. Four areas listed per area; split a human call.
flags: WATERFRONT lead (apply.py doesn't write it): stored 'not waterfront' looks too low. On imagery (160 m frame) the East Shore camping is a gravel lane along the west side of the park road with cars parked 10-25 m from the water across open grass and scattered trees, and a gravel loop on the point north of it (KDWP's East Shore point, 37.39517,-99.78291) with open ground to the water on its west side. The lake is 300 acres at full pool and looked full in the Esri imagery (capture date unknown; it is not one of the lakes KDWP says goes dry). Propose at least LAKEVIEW; LAKEFRONT is arguable for the shore lane, which is itself the camping and has nothing but grass between a parked rig and the water. There are no designated pads to judge from, so I would not go above lakeview without a closer look.

SPLIT data (per area; a human call): KDWP names four areas 0.6-2.6 km apart on different access roads. South End: at the dam (KDWP's point sits on the dam face, 37.38254,-99.78162; a gravel turnaround at the east end of the dam and tracks below it), reached from the southwest county-road entrance; 1.4 km from East Shore. East Shore: the gravel lane and point loop on the east shore, off the park road from K-94 (northeast entrance), with the middle ramp and a picnic shelter; ADA accessible. Bloom Cove: west shore, reached from the northwest county-road entrance (KDWP's point is in the water; the ramp is at 37.39876,-99.78521), 0.6 km across the lake from East Shore but a separate road. North End: the upper end (KDWP's point 37.40597,-99.78529 is in wooded marsh; the only gravel loop I could see is ~150 m south-east at about 37.4049,-99.7838), 0.6 km from Bloom Cove and 1.2 km from East Shore. None has marked sites or posted site counts, so I left this as one entry and recommend keeping it that way unless AWH wants separate pins.

PIN 37.39326,-99.78289 is in the trees east of the paved park road at the middle boat ramp, ~105 m south of the shore camping lane and 213 m from KDWP's East Shore point. Propose 37.3952,-99.7829 (KDWP's East Shore area, the point loop) if a move is wanted; it is just under the 250 m line.

PHONE missing (apply.py doesn't write it): the Clark page lists 'Region Three Office Dodge City, KS (620) 227-8609'; propose it (Pratt Operations Office 620-672-5911 is the statewide line). Website as stored is KDWP's page (403 to plain HTTP; Wayback copy current to July 2026).
MAX STAY: newly written 7 nights (K.A.R. 115-8-9(c)); the Clark page posts no other limit.

ACCESS: East Shore is reached from K-94; Bloom Cove and South End by county gravel roads (KDWP: 'county gravel road'). No 4WD or rig-size statement anywhere; no site lengths published. HOOKUPS (none) left as stored (derived); KDWP types every area 'Primitive Camping'. Restrooms are at the four boat ramps ('Facility w/ Restroom'); type not stated, so facilities left unwritten.
